description.narrative: Oslocentret har inkommit med en ansökan om 15 MSEK för att stödja ett projekt med syfte att stärka de politiska institutionerna för att de ska bli mer lyhörda, ansvarstagande och transparenta i hela valcykeln. Ambassadens samarbetspartner ska stödja sex politiska partier, samt partiregistraren genom dialog, utbildning, framtagande av riktlinjer och andra viktiga dokument. Projektet ska stödja partierna till att utveckla välfungerande partikommittéer på länsnivå, för att kunna bli mer effektiva i att tillvarata medborgarnas intressen och kunna föra en partilinje i länsregeringarna. Skulle den potentiella grundlagsomröstningen bli av är man beredd att inkludera förberedelser inom sina projektpartners för att medborgarnas intressen ska tillvaratas i den processen.

The Oslo Center has submitted a proposal of 15 MSEK to support a project aiming to strengthen political institutions to enhance responsiveness, accountability and transparency in the electorral cycle. The Embassy cooperation partner will work with six political parties, as well as the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties through dialogues, trainings, development of guidelines and other important documents. The project shall support the parties to develop well functioning political party committess in the counties, to enhance efficiency and becoming more responsive to the interests of the citizens, and to speak with 'one party voice' in the county governments.The project is prepared to include preparations of their partners to include the interests of the citizens in the constitutional referendum process, should it be carried out.

The overarching program goal was:
Strengthening Political Institutions to Enhance Responsiveness, Accountability, and Transparency in the Electoral Cycle
The four outcome areas were:
i) County Assembly political parties groups become responsive to the needs of citizens ii) Political parties have operationalised their party constitution in a more accountable and transparent manner iii) To strengthen the office of the Registrar of Political parties (ORPP) to better perform its roles and responsibilities, and iv) Strengthening Women Participation in Political parties' processes and decision making (added in an agreement amendment in December 2019)

In summary, the contribution has enhanced the institutional capacity of political institutions (specifically political parties) in Kenya and increased civic awareness of and citizen engagement in policy-making, which has contributed to increased responsiveness, transparency, accountability and inclusion of political institutions.
Examples of results achieved are:
Outcome 1: Strengthening Political Parties County Elected Members Groups to Respond to the Needs of the Citizens
- Three political party County Assembly Groups (CAGs) were established towards advancing political party policies in the county assemblies (Ford-K, KANU and ANC). Party structures at sub-national level were improved.
- Enhanced responsiveness of county government to citizens needs through the development and adoption of citizen policy priority/manifestos to the County Integrated Development Plans (CIDP).
- Increased civic awareness and responsibility among citizens in Nandi, Mombasa, and Meru counties.
- Some members benefiting from the TOC program were elected into positions at county level.
- The CAGs were instrumental in the division of the revenue bill for 2022/23.
Outcome 2: Promoting Accountability and Transparency by Assisting Parties to Operationalize the Party Constitution
- Strengthened capacity of 2366 party officials to undertake their mandate and responsibilities within seven political parties.
- Strengthened capacity of party organs (National Executive Committees, National Secretariat, Election Boards, Dispute tribunals, Appeals Boards, Disciplinary Committees, Branch committees) among seven political parties.
- Strengthened internal governance structures and party processes of seven political parties resulting in inclusive, accountable, and transparent party processes.
- Improved implementation of party nomination processes resulting in free, credible, and verifiable processes.
- Improved coalition-building processes among political parties.
- Enhanced integration of technology that improved party processes such as membership recruitment, candidate identification, and nomination processes.
- Improved public access to political party documents and information.
Outcome 3: Assistance to Strengthen the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties (ORPP)
- Streamlined ORPPs departmental operations with clear roles and responsibilities enhancing performance, quality, and institutional efficiency.
- Improved risk management in political and electoral environment; identification and mitigation.
- Improved ORPPs management of party membership process through adoption and improvement of the technological infrastructure of the Integrated Political Parties Management System (IPPMS), contributing to effectiveness and increased transparency.
- Improved policy development process by the ORPP, including financial policies and procedures necessary to accommodate the Political Parties Act of 2021.
- A checklist utilized by political parties forming coalitions, critical for the ORPP management of coalitions under the party act.
Outcome 4: Strengthening Women's Participation in Political parties' processes and decision-making
- Institutionalized seven women leagues. Institutional capacity strengthened, including structures, operational and policy documents, legal and administrative documents, compliance with constitutional provisions and women's advocacy.
- Improved capacity of women candidates to participate and effectively compete in elective positions.
- Contributed to knowledge generation hub by undertaking research on barriers to women participation in political and electoral process.
- Increase of women in decision-making organs. This lead to an increase in gender responsive decisions on the representation of women in elective positions during party primaries. There was a significant increase in women candidates in the 2022 elections e.g.:
* In UDA, there was an increase of women appointed to the cabinet. A coalition of women leagues under Kenya Kwanza formation was established to protect the interests of women. The Kenya Kwanza administration appointed 10 women into its 22-member cabinet corresponding to 45%, up from 27% in the previous government. Other parties including JP and KANU recorded an increase in women candidacy.
* The 2022 general elections saw increased women's participation, with 1,962 women out of 14,137 candidates contesting, representing 6.6%, over the previous two electoral cycles, where 932 and 1,300 women, respectively, contested. Seven out of the 47 gubernatorial seats, 26 of the 290 Member of National Assembly seats, and 3 of the 47 Senate seats were won by female candidates, considered a breakthrough for women in active politics.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
